sentences.text: Grippia is a genus containing only one known species, Grippia longirostris, which was a small ichthyopterygian measuring approximately 1 to 1.5 meters in length.
Members of this species swam using lateral tail movements similar to those of a modern-day eel.
No skull of Grippia has been found with a snout, making all descriptions of this feature speculative.
Detailed descriptions of the forelimbs were performed in 1998 by Ryosuke Motani, revealing that the species possessed pentadactyl limbs.
The first and fifth metacarpals and phalanges of Grippia are lunate in appearance and concave inward toward the interior carpals.
Analysis of dental remains suggests Grippia practiced an omnivorous feeding style, though this is debated due to the lack of a complete skull.
Grippia is believed to have lived between 250 and 235 million years ago during the Olenekian to Anisian stages of the Early to Mid-Triassic.
This animal inhabited shallow coastal seas located at equatorial latitudes.
It is debated what Grippia ate because existing fossil samples lack a snout, making dietary conclusions highly speculative.
